hints: Count the carbon atoms in the starting bromoalkane and in the final carboxylic acid, what has happened to the chain length?
Recall which nucleophile can replace Br with a carbon-containing group to extend the chain by one carbon.
Think about what functional group hydrolyses in hot aqueous acid to give a carboxylic acid in the second stage.
walkthrough:
**Count carbons and spot chain extension**

Look carefully at the skeletons. Starting material is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ with 3 carbons.

Product is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ with 4 carbons:
$$3 \text{ carbons} \rightarrow 4 \text{ carbons}$$

**Recall the classic two-step route to add one carbon**

The standard way to add one carbon and then make an acid is substitution with cyanide followed by hydrolysis.

$$\text{R-Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{R-CN} + \text{Br}^-$$
$$\text{R-CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{R-CO}_2\text{H} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Apply to this example**

Here $\text{R} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2$. So stage 1 must give the nitrile with the same R group attached to $\text{CN}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$$

options.A: CH3CH2CH2OH is propan-1-ol formed by hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH. It still has only 3 carbons and oxidation would give propanoic acid, not the 4-carbon butanoic acid, so it cannot be the intermediate in a two-stage route.
options.B: CH3CH2CH2CHO is butanal with 4 carbons. It cannot be made directly from 1-bromopropane in one nucleophilic substitution step, and an aldehyde is normally oxidised to an acid with the same carbon number, not formed from a haloalkane this way.
options.C: CH3CH2CN is propanenitrile with only 3 carbons in total. It would come from CH3CH2Br, not from CH3CH2CH2Br. Hydrolysis would give propanoic acid, which is one carbon too short.
options.D: CH3CH2CH2CN is butanenitrile. It is formed by nucleophilic substitution of Br by CN- using KCN in ethanol, extending the chain from 3 to 4 carbons. Hot aqueous acid hydrolysis then gives CH3CH2CH2CO2H, exactly the required two-stage synthesis.
